reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator promotes KuCoin by claiming holders receive a share of trading profits, describes the arrangement as producing substantial returns, and advises viewers to buy at least $100 of KuCoin. He also directs interested viewers to sign up through a linked destination, creating a concrete investment and referral solicitation rather than merely reporting on cryptocurrency. The video additionally compares the opportunity favorably with BitConnectX and says it expects that project to pay more.

opening.argument: The presentation is qualified commentary, not a guaranteed-return pitch. The speaker repeatedly uses uncertainty, including “Hopefully not too fast,” “we'll see what happens,” and “it is not likely to get even a lot of bonuses from 100 dollar worth of investment.” The description also expressly says, “This video should not be taken as financial advice.” Those qualifications matter: viewers are told that market movement and bonus size are uncertain, and the speaker does not promise that a $100 purchase will produce a particular return.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution emphasizes the 50% description and the speaker's proposed purchase, but it omits the surrounding uncertainty and warning. The speaker expressly says a $100 holding is unlikely to generate much bonus, and the description rejects treating the video as financial advice. That is inconsistent with presenting a dependable profit guarantee.

citations.quote: it is not likely to get even a lot of bonuses from 100 dollar worth of investment to KuCoin.
This video should not be taken as financial advice.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer cannot erase the video's operative message. The speaker still describes holders receiving 50% of trading profits every 24 hours and says, “I will buy at least 100 dollar KuCoin.” Saying that a particular purchase may yield little does not negate soliciting the purchase or presenting the recurring bonus mechanism.

citations.quote: every KuCoin holder gets a split of that profit and that split out actually equals to 50%

opening.argument: The video's central activity is explaining how KuCoin works and demonstrating its surrounding materials. The speaker asks, “what is KU coin,” compares it with other exchanges, explains the bonus calculation, and displays the KuCoin site, market data, and whitepaper. The account is educational and operational: viewers are shown where listings and bonus information appear, including the qualification that the bonus depends on assets held and trading fees. Describing a platform's mechanics and showing documentation is not, by itself, proof that the creator is certifying an investment outcome.

citations.quote: Today I want to talk to you guys about KU coin so what is KU coin.
the amount of cool coin bonus is calculated based on the amount of asset held at midnight on a daily basis

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats explanation as solicitation, but the material is structured around showing viewers what KuCoin is, how its bonus is calculated, and where new listings can be found. The whitepaper and bonus interface are visible source materials, while the speaker also explains limitations on small holdings. A tutorial can discuss a claimed feature without certifying that it is safe or profitable.

citations.quote: the amount of cool coin bonus is calculated based on the amount of asset held at midnight on a daily basis

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing does not change the call to acquire the token. The speaker moves from explaining the mechanism to recommending a minimum holding and supplies a KuCoin sign-up link. Showing a whitepaper or interface makes the pitch more concrete; it does not show that the claimed returns are merely neutral subject matter.

opening.argument: The evidence is consistent with ordinary promotion of an exchange service and its loyalty-style bonus, not a demonstrated scam mechanism. KuCoin is described as “a trading platform,” and the video discusses access to newly listed coins and exchange functionality. The supplied material does not establish a deposit demand, credential request, downline scheme, or guaranteed personal return. It also shows a KuCoin bonus interface and market listings, which are ordinary service features. A referral link may support sign-up, but referral promotion alone does not establish that the underlying service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: is a trading platform that like Binance, just like Bittrex

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution identifies a token, a bonus description, and a sign-up link, but those features also occur in ordinary exchange promotion. Its quotations do not show that viewers were required to transfer funds to the creator, recruit others, surrender credentials, or receive a guaranteed return. The video instead discusses trading access and the practical availability of listings.

citations.quote: The only way to get them is on coocoin
I do have the link where you guys to sign up on KuCoin if you're interested

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing-mechanism argument overlooks the mechanism actually described: holders must keep KuCoin on the exchange to receive a share of trading profits, and the speaker recommends buying at least $100. A scam need not involve recruitment or credentials when the alleged inducement is token appreciation or recurring dividends. The sign-up link makes the promotion actionable.
